questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Assume that ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?

I. The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions.

II. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent.

III. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly dependent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 6 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statement II is false, while statements I and III are true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Assume that ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?

I. The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has only the trivial solution ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$

II. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly dependent.

III. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=0
$$

and, substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

Since ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0$, we get that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.

Therefore, statements I and III are true, while statement II is false.

questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $3{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3}=0.$

II. ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$

III. The set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly dependent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3} & =3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -14 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6-4-2 \\ 9+5-14 \\ -3+3+0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since statement I is true, we have ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ for ${x}_{1}=3,\,{x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=2.$

- Statement III is true. Since statement II is false, the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly *dependent*.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}+3{a}_{3}=0.$

II. ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$

III. The set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}+3{a}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -9 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-8+6 \\ -1+10-9 \\ 7+2-9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since statement I is true, we have ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ for ${x}_{1}=1,\,{x}_{2}=2$ and ${x}_{3}=3.$

- Statement III is false. Since statement II is false, the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly *dependent*.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
